ICS: Needs Work for Level: Interrupts patients/family, does not use silence, gives too much information, is falsely reassuring, becomes defensive
Adequate for Level: Listened carefully and used silence, avoided false reassurance, didn’t give too much information without permission, uses some NURSE (naming, understanding, emotions)

Proficient: Listens, Responds to emotion (names, understands, responds, supports and explores emotion) uses silence, warning shots and body language effectively; Avoided false reassurance, paces conversation well, asked permission before providing information

Positive Response: Utilizes ask-tell-ask to find out what Camilla knows and what she expects before giving much information. Explores how she is feeling. Names the emotion that is seen, restate its, “I can see how frightened you are.” Remembers to ask if it is okay to start giving information. Gives information in small bits. Asks Camilla to repeat/explain what she has heard (i.e. Explores her understanding of what is going on and what the future may hold.)
Negative Response: Student delivers news about brain injury showing no awareness of Camilla's state

Positive Response: Takes time to listen. Doesn’t interfere when the family tries to blame the student. Utilizes silence. Uses an empathic statement “I know it’s hard for you to see Alonzo like this” or “I wish this was different than it is.” Ask when it is okay to give information, and give it in small bits. Ask Camilla to share what she has heard (in a non-defensive way) by setting it up, “Sometimes when all of this is going on, and people are so stressed, we say things that people don’t quite understand, can you tell me what you heard me say?”
Negative Response: Student is defensive, deflects responsibility to others. Accuses Camilla or asks leading questions, or does not identify emotions driving Camilla’s reactions to situation.
